newsitem.title: USA: PHLX mum on reports of probe of chairman.
newsitem.headline: PHLX mum on reports of probe of chairman.

text.p: The Philadelphia Stock Exchange (PHLX) declined comment on media reports it was investigating Chairman Vincent Casella over ties to a company holding a major contract with the exchange.

Exchange spokeswoman Lynda Caravello said she could not comment beyond a statement in which the exchange says it had hired an outside counsel to help it "review certain facts" regarding the relationship of "certain of its members" to the provider of a new trading system.

"In due course, a full report will be made to PHLX's Board of Governors," the statement said. "No conclusions have been drawn regarding the facts in this matter, and the exchange urgers others to do the same."

Media reports have identified Casella as being the focus of the investigation. The Philadelphia Inquirer cited federal documents showing Casella owned 152,000 shares in Ashton Technology Group Inc as of March 31.

On May 2, Ashton went public, and documents listed its contract with the Philadelphia exchange as a major asset, the Inquirer said. An Ashton subsidiary is developing an electronic trading and pricing system for the exchange, it said.

The Inquirer also cited a letter from Casella to the exchange's 505 members and board of governors as saying his actions were "totally motivated," by the "best interests of the exchange" and that "rumors and innuendo" about his ties were based in political infighting within the exchange.

Casella said in the letter that a firm in which he is a principal received 400,000 shares in Ashton for consulting work and a $100,000 loan, the Inquirer said. The shares were then distributed among four Medford partners.
The letter also reportedly said members of exchange committees had discussed the contract with Ashton and agreed to it.
